title: Are there any real world games using Inworld ai ?
author: anchit_rana
selftext: Hi, I have heard about inworld ai, and how they help the creators by saving their time upon the AI stuff. But since the cost of hosting LLM models for games is high, I wonder if there are any ready to play games using this technology?

comments.author: fisj
comments.body: I have no idea what inworld AI is, but if I were to develop a game using AI, I certainly wouldn't be using expensive 3rd party AI services. I highly recommend learning to develop with free and open source tools and models, it will pay off both in developing your own skills and monetarily.

replies.author: anchit_rana
replies.body:
The services they provide are not easy to develop in a certain time frame, and even then hosting costs are too much to bear. you need to have an entire architecture to host LLMs and TTS models. They do it in an optimized way.  
I am not related to them anyhow. I am also a developer who is developing my in-house stuff. Just checking if the world is using their services as they have mentioned in their blogs.

replies.author: littleredscar
replies.body: I think Future for sure. When is the question. Personally, I would definitely pay a little extra to talk to well designed characters in games. As a first step, I’m hoping game studios can incorporate this as an extra mechanic instead of the core mechanic first. The first reason is that it’s probably hard to get it right the first time and a game would be unplayable if AI is the core mechanic and it’s not done well. Secondly, for games like rpgs that I already enjoy, I would for sure like to pay a little extra for them to spice up one or two aspects around character interactions.

replies.author: anchit_rana
replies.body: So what would be a better game? a game with a fixed story but with multiple endings with AI NPCs trained not to go away from the story? Or where the user can set the initial story of the world and then the AI NPCs will unfold the world based on the actions, quite a fantasy game. My guess is that they will both be in use.

comments.author: VinayXDD
comments.body: That's a good question about the use and cost-effectiveness of Inworld AI in practical game settings. Given the expenses tied to hosting LLM models, finding a balance between cost and benefit is pretty crucial for developers. On a similar note, when I was experimenting with building an interactive 3D world, I used Tesana, which allowed me to start with a basic text description and get a workable prototype. It was less fragile when transitioning between development stages. While not specifically the same as hosting an LLM model, the concept of balancing cost and output does seem to resonate across different AI integration methods in game development. Would love to see how others are leveraging these technologies efficiently.
